clue.text: Two british monarchs combined to book the turn of the 13

definitions.text: to book the turn of the 13
definitions.note: the man who put into a book The Turn of the Screw, 13-across giving the last word of the title; a verb phrase standing for its author

parts.note: Henry is the name of eight English kings
James is the name of kings of England, Scotland and Britain

explanation.surface: Two kings join forces to write a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The 13 is a cross-reference: 13-across is SCREW, so 'the turn of the 13' is the ghost story The Turn of the Screw, and the definition names the novelist who wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: The American-born novelist wrote the ghost story The Turn of the Screw in 1898.

clue.text: Went quickly-to keep out of sight, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word for keeping out of sight is spoken, and we write down what we hear

parts.note: to keep out of sight is to hide

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off to avoid being seen, so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hie is an old verb meaning to hurry, so its past tense means hurried.

clue.text: A bare existence keeps one healthy, they claim

definitions.text: A bare existence keeps one healthy, they claim

parts.words: A bare existence keeps one healthy, they claim
parts.note: read 'bare' literally: people who live without clothes and say it does them good

explanation.surface: Some people insist that living simply is good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists go without clothing and often argue the practice is healthy.

clue.text: Lay back on rising at international conference centre

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word lay from end to start
rising, in a down clue, means the word at is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Someone lies back at a big diplomatic summit.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY turned back gives YAL and AT turned up gives TA; 'on' simply joins them. Yalta, in Crimea, hosted the 1945 Allied summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean resort hosted the 1945 summit of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.

clue.text: Directions for delivery of discourse

definitions.meaning: the details written on a letter so the postman knows where to take it
a formal speech given to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the location written on an envelope and a formal speech.

clue.text: Old Ireland with affirmative Furies

parts.note: Erin is an old poetic name for Ireland
yes is the affirmative answer

explanation.surface: Ancient Ireland agrees with the avenging spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the avenging goddesses were called by this name before the Romans called them Furies.

clue.text: Soup stirring as a work of art

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of soup are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stirring soup is treated as a masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for work, it names a musical composition or any artistic creation.

clue.text: Earlier religious officer

definitions.meaning: the head of a religious house, below an abbot

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for preceding and the title of a monastery's deputy head.

clue.text: Wordy painter makes C brusque demand for author's autograph

definitions.meaning: a painter of words, someone who letters shop fronts and signs
a curt order to a writer to put their name on something, as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into SIGN, WRITER! and it is the curt order a fan might bark at a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who paints lettering on boards; split in two it is a curt order telling an author to put pen to paper.

clue.text: A beating can be so embarrassing

parts.note: a beating is a bashing

explanation.surface: Getting a thrashing can be humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone ashamed, so this form means shaming.

clue.text: Former lot returning praise

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: returning means the word lot is read backwards

explanation.surface: An old group comes back to give compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or speak highly of something.

clue.text: Running at the mouth — of the goal?

definitions.text: Running at the mouth — of the goal?

parts.words: Running at the mouth — of the goal?
parts.note: first read as drooling from the mouth, then as running with the ball towards the goalmouth in football

explanation.surface: Someone is drooling, or is it a footballer near the goal?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both letting saliva run from the lips and running with a ball at your feet.

clue.text: In a fancy way, otherwise neatly disordered

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you will miss it'

indicators.note: disordered means the letters of neatly are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something is fancy, or else tidily messed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes something done with elaborate decoration.

clue.text: Vulgar salary for a common prison warder

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word means both a wage and a jailer.

clue.text: Offer a helping hand or forfeit a limb

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to help someone advance
read literally as handing over one of your legs

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to help someone up or along; taken literally it means handing over a leg.

clue.text: Little creepers in religious groups

parts.note: sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: Small sneaky types inside religious bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Small crawling bugs such as beetles and ants creep along the ground.

clue.text: Side-cars could be the making a of Shakespeare's false heroine

indicators.note: the letters of side-cars could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Motorbike sidecars might be the making of a Shakespearean character.
explanation.definitionFit: In Troilus and Cressida the Trojan woman betrays her lover Troilus.

clue.text: Incentives limit us when incorrectly distributed

indicators.note: incorrectly distributed means the letters of limit us are shared out in a new order

explanation.surface: Rewards restrict us when handed out unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that spur action, as incentives do.

clue.text: In negotiations it's the very last word

definitions.text: In negotiations it's the very last word

parts.words: In negotiations it's the very last word
parts.note: the final demand in talks, after which there is no further discussion

explanation.surface: In bargaining, this is the final statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A final demand whose rejection ends talks, often with a threat attached.

clue.text: Your simplest clue?

parts.note: the clue asks for the superlative of simple, a plain description of how this clue reads

explanation.surface: The setter offers the solver an easy one.
explanation.definitionFit: The most simple thing is the least difficult.

clue.text: Jungle drums owned by the piper's son?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme begins 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son', so his name is given twice
owned by points to the possessive ending 's

explanation.surface: Drums belonging to the boy in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son' supplies TOM TOM; adding the possessive S gives the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom-toms are tall hand-beaten drums associated with tribal music.

clue.text: One who benefits from a willing deed

definitions.text: One who benefits from a willing deed

parts.words: One who benefits from a willing deed
parts.note: read 'willing' as making a will: someone who gains under a person's will

explanation.surface: Someone who profits from a generous act.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who receives a bequest under a will.

clue.text: Classical swimmer who earned a Hero's welcome

definitions.text: Classical swimmer who earned a Hero's welcome

parts.words: Classical swimmer who earned a Hero's welcome
parts.note: in Greek myth a youth swam the Hellespont nightly to be welcomed by his lover Hero

explanation.surface: An ancient swimmer got a celebrity reception.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend he swam the Hellespont every night to visit the priestess Hero.

clue.text: Hebridean gunman

definitions.meaning: an island of the Outer Hebrides off Scotland
the ... gun was named after its inventor, Isaac Newton ...

explanation.definitionFit: The name is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides and the inventor of a First World War machine gun.

clue.text: It sounds correct in order to 108

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'It sounds correct in order to 108', ends in a garbled cross-reference ('108'); WRITE sounds like RIGHT (correct) but the definition cannot be recovered.
annotationWithheld.clue: It sounds correct in order to 108

clue.text: Parsimonious period in the interim

parts.note: parsimonious means mean or stingy
a period is a time

explanation.surface: A stingy spell while we wait.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'in the meantime' means during the interval in between.

clue.text: Keepsake to recognise in Scotland

parts.note: ken is the Scots verb for know or recognise

explanation.surface: A memento to remember the Scots by.
explanation.definitionFit: A small object kept as a reminder, a souvenir.

clue.text: His work is colourful in a gaudy, erratic style

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An artist works in a flashy, unpredictable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who colours cloth for a trade.

clue.text: Where fraternal craftsmen may cross the water in Surrey

parts.note: a guild is a brotherhood of craftsmen
to ford is to cross a river by wading

explanation.surface: A place where brotherhoods of artisans wade across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: GUILDFORD is the county town of Surrey, a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral town is Surrey's county town on the River Wey.

clue.text: The girl in the pool

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, short for Katherine
a shared fund of money, as in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: It is a pet form of Katherine and a fund of pooled money.

clue.text: Skinny resort in the To. M.

definitions.meaning: to strip off the skin of a fruit
a seaside town on the west coast of the Isle of Man, printed I.o.M.

explanation.walkthrough: 'To. M.' is the page's misreading of I.o.M., the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to strip the rind from fruit and names a harbour town on the Isle of Man.

clue.text: One with an eye for heavenly bodies or a monster in disguise

definitions.text: One with an eye for heavenly bodies

indicators.note: in disguise means the letters of or a monster are rearranged to hide them

explanation.surface: A stargazer, or perhaps a beast dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies stars and planets through a telescope.
